newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH NFI FIRMS CONSOLIDATION SEEN ON OCT 15.
newsitem.headline: POLISH NFI FIRMS CONSOLIDATION SEEN ON OCT 15.

text.p: Five National Investment Funds (NFIs) in Poland's mass privatisation programme will exchange small minority stakes in several companies to consolidate their holdings, the president of NFI No.6 said on Friday.

Krzysztof Bialowolski said his fund and four other NFIs signed a deal to exchange the 1.93-percent minority stakes so that the funds could hold eight-to-ten-percent stakes in firms and thereby reduce the number of firms under their management.
"Five NFIs signed a deal on consolidating firms' minority stakes, and one other -- NFI No. 11 -- has declared to join," he told Reuters, adding the consolidation was set for Tuesday.
The privatisation programme's 15 NFIs manage 514 companies.

About 28 million adult Poles are entitled to buy an NFI certificate for 20 zloty to later be exchanged for shares in the funds, which are expected to enter the Warsaw bourse in the first quarter of 1997.
Each of the 15 NFIs began the programme with strategic 33-percent stakes in 33 to 35 companies and 1.93 percent of the remaining firms.
The remaining shares of companies taking part in the programme are divided between the state treasury, which has 25 percent, and employees, who hold 15 percent.
Bialowolski said that in the consolidation operation the funds holding strategic stakes would not be allowed to boost their 33-percent ownership.
